findings.explanation: The new DELETE /users/<id> endpoint (app/routes/users.py:56-66) is gated only by @require_auth, which merely authenticates and sets g.current_user (app/auth.py:55-66) and performs no role check. Policy §2 states 'Deleting a user account requires the **admin** role' and api-spec.md lists 'DELETE /users/<id> | admin only'. The handler fetches and deletes a user by the user-controlled user_id with no @require_role('admin') gate, so any authenticated user (role 'user') can delete any account. This is a missing authorization check on a newly added endpoint.

evidence.content: Deleting a user account requires the **admin** role.

findings.suggested_fix: Add the @require_role("admin") decorator to delete_user (in addition to or replacing @require_auth), matching the pattern used by admin-only endpoints such as app/routes/admin.py:18-19, so only administrators can delete user accounts.

args.query: require_auth decorator definition and how it sets current user

sections.title: New DELETE /users/<id> endpoint lacks the required admin-role authorization
